plain.text: At dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to the tomb. There was a great earthquake; an angel rolled back the stone and sat on it, and the guards shook with fear. The angel told the women: Do not be afraid. You are looking for Jesus who was crucified. He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Go quickly and tell his disciples. As they ran, afraid yet filled with joy, Jesus met them. They held his feet and worshipped him. He told them to tell his brothers to go to Galilee, where they would see him.

Some of the guards told the chief priests what had happened. The leaders paid them a large sum to say that the disciples had stolen the body while they slept, and promised to keep them out of trouble with the governor. That story was still being told when Matthew wrote.

The eleven disciples went to the mountain in Galilee. When they saw Jesus they worshipped him, but some doubted. Jesus said: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptising them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey all I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.

summary.bigIdea: Jesus is risen, and he sends his followers to make disciples of all nations, promising to be with them always.
points: An angel tells the women that Jesus has risen, just as he said.
The leaders bribe the guards to spread a false story.
Jesus sends his disciples to all nations and promises to be with them always.
summary.reflection: Jesus promises, I am with you always. Where do you most need to hear that today?
